title: A labelled photo at every station
allegory: An activation cache is an assembly line with a camera at every station: run the line once and you get an album with one labelled photo of every in-between step, which you can flip through as often as you like.
map: a HookPoint at every named activation
the ActivationCache: a dictionary from hook names to tensors
the album index: which kind of photo, which station
scribbling on a photo does not change the product
the cache only reads; a hook can write back and change the forward pass

chapters.name: What happened inside?
chapters.note: I only see what comes out

cap.1: You ask the model something and an answer comes out. But the interesting part happened in the middle, and it is gone the moment the run ends.
cap.2: A plain forward pass returns logits and throws every intermediate tensor away. Interpretability needs those in-between values: attention patterns, residual streams, head outputs.
cap.3: Intermediate activations are transient in a standard forward pass. Mech interp needs them materialised and addressable by name, per layer and per component.

cap.1: Picture an assembly line with a camera at every station. Run the line once and you get an album: one labelled photo of every in-between step.
cap.2: logits, cache = model.run_with_cache(tokens) runs once and hands back every intermediate activation, stored in a dictionary under its name.
cap.3: run_with_cache attaches a caching function at every HookPoint and returns an ActivationCache: a dict-like map from hook names to tensors for that one forward pass.

cap.1: Every photo has a full label, like blocks.0.attn.hook_pattern. You can ask for it the short way: which kind of photo, at which station.
cap.2: The cache is keyed by hook names. cache['pattern', 0] is shorthand that utils.get_act_name expands to 'blocks.0.attn.hook_pattern'.
cap.3: Names follow one scheme across 140+ architecture families, so code written for GPT-2 small transfers. For a single sequence, remove_batch_dim=True drops the batch axis.

chapters.name: Check the photos
chapters.title: a layer-0 attention pattern (toy values): does it pass the checks?

cap.1: Trust, but check. Rebuild one photo from the others and see that it matches. Here: every row adds up to 1, and no word looks at the future.
cap.2: Verifying activations: recompute one (say layer 0's pattern from the cached queries and keys) and compare with the cached tensor. Rows sum to 1; the upper triangle is 0.
cap.3: A pattern is softmax over scaled, causally masked QKᵀ, so rows are distributions and entries above the diagonal vanish. Recomputing from hook_q and hook_k should reproduce hook_pattern.

chapters.name: Photos change nothing
chapters.verdict: The cache observes; a hook intervenes.

cap.1: Scribbling on a photo does not change what came off the line. To change the product you need a hand on the line itself, not a camera.
cap.2: Editing a cached tensor changes nothing about the model's output. To intervene, use run_with_hooks with a function that writes a new value during the run.
cap.3: The cache is a post hoc, read-only record. Causal methods (ablation, activation patching, steering) need hooks that return modified activations mid-forward.

chapters.name: Why it matters
items: Every attention pattern you plot comes from here
Patching: cache a clean run, write it into another

cap.1: Almost every look inside a model starts with one cached run. It is the album you flip through to understand what the model did, before you try to steer it.
cap.2: Attention patterns, the logit lens and direct logit attribution all read from the cache. Activation patching caches a clean run, then hooks write those values into a corrupted one.
cap.3: The cache is the observational layer of mech interp; causal methods pair it with hooks that write back. Understanding a model comes before steering it.

coda.title: Rows are layers 0 to 3; columns are resid_pre, q, pattern, z, mlp_out. Tap to look a photo up.

readouts.label: full hook names
readouts.f: G.flatMap((row, L) => row.map((v, k) => v ? 'blocks.' + L + '.' + ['hook_resid_pre', 'attn.hook_q', 'attn.hook_pattern', 'attn.hook_z', 'hook_mlp_out'][k] : '')).filter(s => s).join(', ') || 'tap a cell'

readouts.label: cache shorthand
readouts.f: G.flatMap((row, L) => row.map((v, k) => v ? "cache['" + ['resid_pre', 'q', 'pattern', 'z', 'mlp_out'][k] + "', " + L + ']' : '')).filter(s => s).join(', ') || 'tap a cell'

readouts.label: photos picked
readouts.f: G.flat().filter(v => v).length + ' of 20, all from one run'

caption.1: Rows are layers, columns are kinds of photo. Tap a few cells and read the exact labels you would look them up by. Spot the pattern in the names.
caption.2: Each tap shows the full hook name and its cache shorthand. The recipe is blocks.<layer>.<where>.hook_<what>, the same for every model TransformerLens loads.
caption.3: Names compose layer, submodule and activation, and get_act_name maps (name, layer) onto them. q, pattern and z sit under attn; resid_pre and mlp_out hang off the block.

where_else: Activation patching: cache a clean run, then write its values into a corrupted run with hooks
Attention-pattern plots: read straight out of cache['pattern', layer]
Logit lens and direct logit attribution: unembed cached residual streams and head outputs
Outside ML: flight recorders and request tracing keep every stage of one run for later

hamming.what: One forward pass that also returns every intermediate activation, stored in a dictionary under its hook name.
hamming.when: At the start of almost every interpretability experiment, whenever you want to see what happened inside a run.
hamming.why: The in-between values are where the model's mechanism lives, and having them all by name turns 'what did the model do?' into a lookup.

object.title: The camera line
object.subtitle: A forward pass as a line of stations on one stream, with a named camera at every junction.

cap.1: One run down the line. The tube is the stream every station reads from and writes to, and a camera sits at every junction.
cap.2: Blocks are components; junctions are named HookPoints; run_with_cache photographs every one of them.
cap.3: HookPoints wrap each activation (resid_pre, q, k, v, pattern, z, attn_out, mlp_out, resid_post), all captured in one cached forward.

cap.1: Zoom into a station: inside attention there are more cameras, for the queries, the keys, the pattern and each head's output.
cap.2: blocks.0.attn holds hook_q, hook_k, hook_v, hook_pattern and hook_z, so you can see inside a layer, not just between layers.
cap.3: Hooking activations rather than modules, inspired by Anthropic's Garcon ProbePoints, is what lets you read values computed partway through a layer.

cap.1: Every photo gets its label from the same recipe, so you can find any of them later without running the line again.
cap.2: One naming scheme across 140+ architecture families: code written against GPT-2 transfers to other models.
cap.3: HookedTransformer normalises architectures onto one activation-naming scheme; ActivationCache keys resolve through utils.get_act_name.

cap.1: The album is a record, not a remote control. Scribbling on a photo changes nothing that came off the line.
cap.2: Editing a cached tensor leaves the run untouched. To intervene, attach a hook that writes back during the forward pass.
cap.3: The cache is read-only with respect to the computation; interventions need run_with_hooks with functions that return modified activations.

predict.q: You edit cache['pattern', 0] in place. Does the model's output change?

options.t: No: the cache is a record of a finished run
Yes: the cache feeds back into the model

predict.why: The cache reads and stores. To change a forward pass you need a hook that writes back while it runs.
utils.get_act_name turns ('pattern', 0) into the full hook name blocks.0.attn.hook_pattern.

predict.q: How many forward passes does run_with_cache need to capture every layer?
predict.why: It attaches a caching function at every hook point and records them all during a single run.
